definition: A protocol that encrypts DNS queries by sending them over HTTPS connections, preventing third parties from seeing which websites you're trying to visit.
metaDescription: Learn about DNS over HTTPS (DoH), a privacy protocol that encrypts your web browsing requests to prevent surveillance and tampering.
simpleExplanation: When you visit a website, your device first asks a DNS server for the website's address. DNS over HTTPS encrypts this request, so your internet provider or others can't see which sites you're looking up.
whyItMatters: Without DoH, your DNS queries are sent in plain text, allowing ISPs, governments, or hackers to monitor your browsing habits, block websites, or redirect you to malicious sites. DoH protects this communication.
technicalDetail: DoH encapsulates DNS queries within HTTPS requests to port 443, using the same encryption that protects web traffic. This makes DNS traffic indistinguishable from regular web browsing, preventing network-level filtering and providing authentication of the DNS resolver.

examples.explanation: When using airport WiFi, DoH prevents the network operator from seeing that you're looking up your bank's website or blocking access to certain news sites.
Your internet provider can't see that you're visiting social media sites or streaming services when DoH is enabled, preventing them from throttling or monitoring your activity.
In countries that block websites by filtering DNS requests, DoH can help bypass these restrictions by encrypting your DNS lookups.
